root.note: The day name is certain. Where the name of the god Saturn comes from is not known; it may be Etruscan.

history: Saturday is the only English day of the week with a Roman god in its name. For the other days, the Anglo-Saxons put their own gods in place of the Roman ones: Tiw for Mars, Woden for Mercury, Thunor for Jupiter, Frige for Venus. For Saturn they seem to have had no match, so they kept him: Latin Saturni dies became Old English Sæternesdæg. Dutch zaterdag and West Frisian saterdei have the same Roman god. Many other languages named the day after the Jewish Sabbath (Hebrew shabbat, ‘rest’): German Samstag, French samedi, Spanish sábado, Russian суббота. In the north of Germany, people also say Sonnabend, ‘Sunday eve’.
historyEinfach: Saturday means ‘Saturn's day’. Saturn was a Roman god. The other days have old English gods, like Woden in Wednesday. Only Saturday has a Roman god. In many other languages, the name of this day comes from the Sabbath, the Jewish day of rest.

cognates.note: from the Sabbath, a different word

elsewhere.text: Welsh, spoken in Wales, took all its day names from Latin: dydd Sadwrn is Saturn's day, dydd Mercher is Mercury's day (Wednesday), and dydd Iau is Jupiter's day (Thursday).
German Samstag sounds a bit like Saturday, but it is a different word: it comes from the Sabbath, the Jewish day of rest, like French samedi and Spanish sábado.
